subjects.displayTitle: Beyond prejudice: fairness, fellowship, and the work of equality
subjects.introduction: Prejudice begins small, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes: a few people say something hateful with a fragment of truth in it, the story spreads, the circle widens, and soon there is a schism. From that ordinary beginning come estrangement between races and religions and countries laid waste. He answers with two plain measures. The first is fairness, praised whether it comes from a neighbour or a stranger, since a well-wishing stranger is worth more than an ignorant acquaintance. The second is delight in difference: a garden of one colour has no beauty, and doves and sheep, black and white, never quarrel over their hue. Yet goodwill alone does not uproot what has grown for generations, and the guidance that follows asks a community to examine its own condescension, protect its minorities, and act together. James, watching a gathering honour a rich visitor and seat a poor one on the floor, makes the same test concrete [1]. The road continues into blind imitation, into race unity and love of country, and into the oneness of humanity that gives every effort its reason.
subjects.arc: Begin with how prejudice grows in conversation, move to fairness and the beauty of diversity, then examine inherited assumptions, collective harm, practical fellowship, and responsibility within one’s own community.

order.why: Read the reported comparison with animals that do not quarrel over color.
Test fairness through the well-wishing stranger.
Open with the reported growth of a harmful story into division.
Read differences of color as an adornment of the human garden.
shortened: These differences of color are in truth an adornment. If all flowers in a garden were of one color, what fragrance would it have? But if you see a garden where flowers of different colors have bloomed, it appears supremely delicate and beautiful to behold. Likewise if the human world were of one color what distinction would it possess? But differences of color are the cause of the manifestation of the power of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Explore common human endowments and the rejection of racial inequality.
shortened: In fact numerous points of partnership and agreement exist between the two races; whereas the one point of distinction is that of color. Shall this, the least of all distinctions, be allowed to separate you as races and individuals? In physical bodies, in the law of growth, in sense endowment, intelligence, patriotism, language, citizenship, civilization and religion you are one and the same. A single point of distinction exists -- that of racial color. God is not pleased with -- neither should any reasonable or intelligent man be willing to recognize -- inequality in the races because of this distinction.

order.why: Ground the inquiry in equality before God.
shortened: All these in the presence of God are equal; they are of one race and creation; God did not make these divisions. These distinctions have had their origin in man himself. Therefore, as they are against the plan and purpose of reality, they are false and imaginary.

order.why: Consider the reported power of imagined divisions despite shared humanity.
Read the synagogue address’s appeal to one human family.
Hear the question of making color a cause of strife.
Keep the reported Jack Johnson example in its historical setting.
Consider the invitation to learn from diversity in the vegetable world.
Keep the reported distinction between hatred and prejudice in its historical setting.
Trace prejudice to blind imitation and its social consequences.
shortened: And the breeding-ground of all these tragedies is prejudice: prejudice of race and nation, of religion, of political opinion; and the root cause of prejudice is blind imitation of the past -- imitation in religion, in racial attitudes, in national bias, in politics. So long as this aping of the past persisteth, just so long will the foundations of the social order be blown to the four winds, just so long will humanity be continually exposed to direst peril.

order.why: Read the warning that attachment to religion or personality can blind judgment.
Consider prejudice as an obstacle to realization.
shortened: We must not entertain prejudice, for prejudice is an obstacle to realization. Inasmuch as the effulgence is one effulgence, the human realities must all become recipients of the same light, recognizing in it the compelling force that unites them in its illumination.

order.why: Join deprivation of understanding with the problem of misunderstanding.
shortened: If we harbor prejudice, it will be the cause of deprivation and ignorance.
The strife between religions, nations and races arises from misunderstanding.

order.why: Hear the call to look with the eye of fairness.
Read the removal of prejudice as a test of religion’s purpose.
shortened: Religion must remove prejudice; if it does not eliminate prejudice, it is not religion, for religion is the following of truth.

Therefore we must abandon racial, national, political and religious prejudices and investigate truth, for these prejudices cause differences among humanity. This prejudice causes blood to be shed. This prejudice causes helpless mothers to cry and wail over the death of their children. This prejudice causes fathers to become sonless. This prejudice causes the countries of the world to be laid waste. This prejudice has caused and continues to cause the world's turmoil.

order.why: Keep the reported criticism of religious teaching attributed to its setting.
shortened: The chief cause is the misrepresentation of religion by the religious leaders and teachers. They teach their followers to believe that their own form of religion is the only one pleasing to God, and that followers of any other persuasion are condemned by the All-Loving Father and deprived of His Mercy and Grace. Hence arise among the peoples, disapproval, contempt, disputes and hatred.

order.why: Read religious antagonism beside the unity attributed to the Founders.
shortened: One of the forms of prejudice which afflict the world of mankind is religious bigotry and fanaticism. When this hatred burns in human hearts, it becomes the cause of revolution, destruction, abasement of humankind and deprivation of the mercy of God. For the holy Manifestations and divine Founders of religion Themselves were completely unified in love and agreement, whereas Their followers are characterized by bitter antagonism and attitudes of hostility toward each other.

order.why: Consider the reported distinction between human inventions and religious foundations.
shortened: And soon these prejudices and rotten traditions will pass away for these traditions and superstitions are the cause of difference and strife. They have no connection to divine religion - they are human inventions, not the foundation of the divine Manifestations. The foundation of divine religions is sanctified and free from these superstitions, especially in this luminous age when most have realized that these superstitions are fruitless and harmful to the comfort and ease of humanity.

order.why: Retain the historical account of exclusion from a home in its own voice.
shortened: The hatred between nations was such that they considered each other unclean. If a Jew entered a Muslim's house, they would make him sit on the ground considering him unclean, and if he drank from a cup, they would either break it or wash it repeatedly.

order.why: Keep the synagogue address’s diagnosis of religious enmity contextualized.
Retain the reported comparison among churches without turning it into a present-day generalization.
Hear the reported challenge to dogmatic superiority.
Keep the reported judgment of a community attributed rather than generalizing it.
Read the reported condemnation of sectarian killing.
shortened: The basic reason for this slaughter is the division between religions - each sect considering the religion of others as barbarous and each deeming it a most sacred trust to shed the blood of the infidels.

order.why: Consider the reported criticism of coercion disguised as salvation.
Read the reported consequences of misinterpreting divine commands.
shortened: Misinterpreting the divine commands, men have acquired prejudices and on these prejudices they have waged religious wars and caused bloodshed. Behold what is happening to-day! Men are killing their brothers, believing this to be the cause of salvation, believing that such work is approved by God, believing that those whom they kill will be sent to hell.

order.why: Retain the brief reported observation about religious education in its source context.
Keep the reported description of the Orient as historical rhetoric with its omission visible.
Question boundaries through the public address’s image of a shared homeland.
shortened: Why should dissension exist among them? The surface of the earth is one native land, and that native land was provided for all. God has not set these boundaries and race limitations. Why should imaginary barriers which God has not originally destined be made a cause of contention?

order.why: Read the address’s sweeping account of warfare as its stated argument.
Retain the related reported causal claim in its own voice.
Consider the address to the Japanese YMCA through East-West association.
Read prejudice as a barrier to human development and welfare.
Hear the Peace Society address’s account of the body politic.
shortened: He pronounced prejudice -- whether religious, racial, patriotic, political -- the destroyer of the body politic. He said that man must recognize the oneness of humanity, for all in origin belong to the same household, and all are servants of the same God.

order.why: Keep the Metaphysical Club address’s historical generalization attributed.
Read the reported appeal to one country and one race.
Consider the reported classification of causes of disputes.
Keep the reported address to socialists in its own setting.
Read the reported inquiry into the causes of bloodshed.
Hear the reported consequences for homes and human lives.
Connect the assembly’s principles with displacement and the Balkan conflict.
Keep the wartime reference to racial prejudice and commercial rivalry attributed.
Read the reported warning about American racial conflict as a historical warning.
shortened: If the races do not come to an agreement, there can be no question or doubt of bloodshed. When I was in America, I told the white and colored people that it was incumbent upon them to be united or else there would be the shedding of blood. I did not say more than this so that they might not be saddened. But, indeed, there is a greater danger than only the shedding of blood. It is the destruction of America.

order.why: Retain the reported criticism of prejudice and self-interest in the East.
shortened: Religious prejudices from one side, the darkness of racial fanaticism from another, political prejudices from another side, ignorant prejudices from another side, self-attachment and personal interests and motives-all these have made the horizons of the East darker than night.

order.why: Read ignorance and ideological division together.
Consider prejudice among the obstacles to shared happiness.
shortened: It is the wish of our heavenly Father that every heart should rejoice and be filled with happiness, that we should live together in felicity and joy. The obstacle to human happiness is racial or religious prejudice, the competitive struggle for existence and inhumanity toward each other.

order.why: Hear the call for freedom from destructive distinctions.
Read outward civilization beside continuing fanaticism.
Retain the concise teaching concerning destructive prejudice.
shortened: Fifth is that religious prejudice, racial prejudice, national prejudice, political prejudice destroy the foundation of humanity and cause the wrath and anger of God.

order.why: Consider service to morals through rejecting political and patriotic prejudice.
Explains the destructive effects of religious, racial, political and other prejudices.
Extend the inquiry into commercial, industrial, and agricultural relations.
Retain the inclusion of economic prejudice.
shortened: They abrogate and nullify religious, racial, political, patriotic and economic prejudices and the like.

order.why: Hear the wish to be free of the several named prejudices.
Place the principle beside investigation, science, equality, language, and justice.
Read the reported public message through education, economic conditions, and universal rights.
Consider the related account of reasoning across social and spiritual principles.
Read the prayer for a church’s service to unity and equality.
Hear the reported call to work for peace and the rights of women and men.
Read teaching through the oneness of humanity and mutual attraction.
Make the principle a requirement of lived service.
Consider the reported invitation to enter one another’s places of worship.
Read the reported refusal of separation based on dogma.
shortened: The Mohammedans must go to the churches of the Christians and of the Jews and vice-versa, the others must go to the Mohammedan mosques. They hold aloof from one another merely because of unfounded prejudices and dogmas.

order.why: Consider fellowship among people of different religions and places.
Hear the reported hope for growing connections.
Read the reported interview’s emphasis on interdependence and universal love.
Consider the reported description of service through oneness and peace.
Read connection and harmony across religions and peoples.
Consider a Spiritual Assembly’s responsibility for unity and understanding.
shortened: As for the Spiritual Assembly, I pray that God may assist them in all affairs and enable them to exalt the Word of God and promote the divine teachings, so that they may become the cause of human unity and the spread of the divine breaths, until no prejudice remains between religions, denominations and races, and all may hold fast together to the cord of God, and misunderstandings between all parties may vanish, and the human world may become a mirror of the Kingdom of God upon which spiritual lights shine.

order.why: Read the prayer for an enduring institution bearing fruits of friendship.
Follow the movement from persecution and estrangement toward affection and reconciliation.
Keep the reported hope for how a community’s conduct will be recognized by others.
Read service as helping communities grow together.
Consider the personal acknowledgment of service against economic and other prejudices.
Keep the personal address concerning Covenant and goodwill in its own setting.
shortened: The letter brought joy, for its contents indicated that you are protected and preserved from the evil of the Covenant-breakers, that you are explaining the divine teachings, serving the unity of the human world, are free from the ignorant prejudices that are ingrained in nations and peoples, and are a well-wisher of all humanity.

order.why: Hear the wish that a person become a source of illumination.
Retain the reported hope for unity across creeds and nations.
shortened: My hope is that the Divine Light may shine here, and that the Heavenly Star of Baha'u'llah may strengthen you, so that you may be the cause of the Oneness of Humanity, that you may help to make the darkness of superstition and prejudice disappear and unite all creeds and all nations.

order.why: Keep the particular address concerning Germany in its historical setting.
Read the hope for receptivity amid wartime upheaval.
shortened: From these wartime upheavals, a wonderful capacity has been created among people. The divine teachings are the spirit of this age, and ears are ready to hear, so that, God willing, the unity of the human world will pitch its tent at the pole of the horizons, and these religious, sectarian, racial and even national prejudices will be eliminated.

order.why: Hear the call to gather beneath the banner of unity.
Read peace and freedom from prejudice together.
Retain the direct counsel to avoid inherited enmity.
Keep the parallel counsel in its separate wording.
shortened: O ye believers of God! Avoid the smell of ignorant prejudices, the blind enmity and hatred and the racial, patriotic and religious superstitions which are in toto inconsistent with the Divine Religion, opposed to the good-pleasure of God and conducive to the deprivation of man from the Bestowals of the Merciful.

order.why: Read the concise enumeration of prejudices to abandon.
Hear the reported appeal to abandon all named forms.
shortened: We must abandon all forms of prejudices - religious, racial, sectarian, patriotic and nationalistic.

order.why: Read the reported relation between Gospel practice and Baha’i teaching.
Consider the reported answer that unity requires removing its obstacles.
Read the reported paradox of a captivity that frees from prejudice.
shortened: It has always been the practice of the heedless to hold back the sincere ones from the Cause of God. As for a trap, praise be to God that we have been trapped happily for sixty years and we have no desire to escape. It is a trap that frees people from the shackles of prejudice and superstitions and delivers them from the prison of self and desire. It makes them the captives of the love of God and of service to the Cause of the oneness of humanity.

order.why: Keep the reported reliance on divine power in view.
shortened: The divine power alone is potent enough to triumph over these religious, racial and patriotic prejudices.

order.why: Consider the reported image of sunlight and obscuring clouds.
shortened: Fix your eyes on the Sun of Truth for his light floods the whole earth. Let the sun give you of his strength then the clouds of prejudice will not hide his light from your eyes, then will the sun be without clouds for you.

order.why: Hear the prayer concerning the darkness of conflict.
Retain the brief reported call to purify thought.
Keep the reported appeal to the Hidden Words and Tablets.
Read the reported refusal to reduce a person to a religious label.
Hear the ideal of one homeland and freedom from prejudice.
Read the affirmation of Baha’i freedom from prejudice beside the demanding guidance that follows.
Close the linked readings with the reported definition of a Baha’i.
shortened: He said, Tell them a Baha'i is a person who is free from all prejudices—racial prejudices, religious prejudices, political prejudices, social prejudices, economic prejudices.

order.why: Read Shoghi Effendi’s supplied call for individual and concerted action.
Consider the supplied prohibition against discrimination on grounds of minority status.
Read the supplied guidance on protecting minority interests and representation.
Connect recognition of oneness with measures to overcome racism.
End with the supplied call for self-examination and changed community practice, preserving its historical language and omissions.
shortened: "White American Baha'is, he feels, although they have very much less prejudice than the American people, are nevertheless tainted to some extent with this national evil, perhaps wholly unconsciously so. Therefore, it behooves every believer of white extraction to carefully study his own attitude, and to see whether he is condescending in his relations with his fellow-Baha'is of negro extraction . . .

He feels it is time that the Baha'is stopped worrying entirely about the white element in a community, and that they should concentrate on showing the negro element that this is a Faith which produces full equality and which loves and wants minorities. The Baha'is should welcome the negroes to their homes, make every effort to teach them, associate with them, even marry them if they want to. We must remember that 'Abdu'l-Baha Himself united in Baha'i marriage a colored and a white believer.

questions: How can ordinary conversation turn a fragment of truth into a prejudice, and what might interrupt that process?
What is the difference between valuing human diversity and treating differences as grounds for unequal regard?
How does James 2:1–9 bring the problem of partiality into the everyday arrangements of a religious gathering?
Which inherited assumptions might remain invisible to a community that sincerely professes equality?
How do protection of minorities, institutional action, and personal fellowship contribute different parts of the work?
What would a fair welcome to a stranger reveal about the relationship between belief and practice?

references.label: 1 · James 2:1–9 · An unequal welcome
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of a gathering that gives privileged treatment to a richly dressed visitor and a lesser place to someone poor. Notice the link between partiality and the command to love one’s neighbor. Compare this concrete test of fellowship with the compilation’s calls for fairness, self-examination, and protection of minorities.

subjects.displayTitle: Mirza Yahya and the Azalis: rupture, testimony, and restraint
subjects.introduction: A brother raised under one’s own care, sheltered for twenty years from friend and foe alike, turns in secret to plot one’s death. That is the wound at the heart of Bahá’u’lláh’s account of Mirza Yahya, and the astonishing thing is the reply it drew from Him: no hatred for him or for any created thing, a door closed in the hope that malice might cool, a ban on recrimination among grieving companions, and the Qur’anic refusal to raise a hand against one who would kill [1]. The story asks how a community can remember a rupture truthfully without letting memory breed new enmity. Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá speak of grief, of authority claimed through titles and nominations, of disguises, marriages and intrigue, and they press their hearers to prefer sight to hearsay: go to Cyprus, open the books in London, ask those who were present. Their language is sharp, and it belongs to its time and its anguish. The path leads from here into the life of Bahá’u’lláh and the exile in Adrianople, where the break became public, and on to the Covenant and its breaking, where a later generation met the same test in a new form.
subjects.arc: Begin with nonretaliation, then examine the grief and history of the rupture, the sources of authority, the demands of inquiry, and the ethical responsibility of remembering conflict.

order.why: Open with protection, suffering, refusal of violence, and the invitation to purify the self.
shortened: O My brother, who hast slandered Me after I reared thee by Mine own self and protected thee from the harm of the worlds!

Hear then what was revealed before: "If thou stretch out thine hand to slay Me, I shall not stretch out Mine hand to slay thee. God is witness to what I say." O My brother! By God, thou and those with thee shall perish and return to dust, while sovereignty remaineth with God, the Almighty, the Powerful. By God, O My brother! I harbor no hatred for thee nor for any created thing in My heart. Therefore hear My words, purify thyself, and be not of the heedless.

order.why: Read the prohibition of recrimination and injunction to patience beside the allegation of attempted killing.
shortened: Yet when My brother beheld the rising fame of the Cause, he became filled with arrogance and pride.  Thereupon he emerged from behind the veil of concealment, rose up against Me, disputed My verses, denied My testimony, and repudiated My signs.  Nor would his hunger be appeased unless he were to devour My flesh and drink My blood.

When news spread of that which the promptings of self had impelled My brother to attempt, and Our companions in exile learned of his nefarious design, the voice of their indignation and grief was lifted up and threatened to spread throughout the city.  We forbade, however, such recriminations, and enjoined upon them patience, that they might be of those that endure steadfastly.

order.why: Hear the appeal to fairness through the question of harming any created being.
shortened: Thou hast indeed associated with Me - didst thou ever find Me willing to harm any created thing? Be fair, then, and be of the equitable. Had I desired to harm My brother, was I not able to do so? Yet despite My power over him and My knowledge of his condition, I sheltered him beneath My wing for twenty years, while he would veil his face in fear of both friend and foe.

order.why: Read the claim of continued protection despite the ability to retaliate.
Consider withdrawal as an attempt to calm hatred.
shortened: Then know that after thy departure, We left these people and dwelt alone in the house, closing the door, that perchance thereby the fire of hatred might be stilled in the breasts of the deceivers. Thou knowest that I spoke not a word with my brother nor associated with him. When there appeared from him what he desired and God revealed what was hidden in his breast, he arose with mighty calumny and wrote tablets wherein he attributed to My wronged, lonely, estranged Self what he wished within himself.

order.why: Keep the departure and the safety of children and wives within the same account.
Hear the prayerful expression of grief at betrayal.
Read the distinction between personal grief and followers who did not witness events.
shortened: O handmaid of God!

I have been prevented from engaging in remembrance due to what has befallen Me from My brother and those who followed him, despite their having no knowledge thereof - and God is witness to what I say. Indeed, I have become the target of the arrows of his hatred and rancor, and at every moment there comes upon Me that which causes My soul to grieve. None is aware of this save God, your Lord and the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Consider the reluctance to recount the deeds of someone long protected.
shortened: By God, I am ashamed to mention to you what my brother did - he whom we taught and protected for twenty years. Surely by now news of him has reached those parts. Whoever looks upon his words with the eye of God will recognize him and be among those who know.

order.why: Read concealment of accusations as an effort to protect the Faith.
shortened: By God the Truth, had My blood been shed a thousand times, it would have been better in My sight than for these matters to become known among the servants.

Verily I was cognizant of what was within his soul from former times, yet We concealed it lest it cause the feet of the deluded ones to stumble. When that which was manifest appeared from him, I commanded that the people be informed, that their faith might be preserved and their deeds not be rendered vain, lest they be numbered among the lost.

order.why: Place that restraint beside the source’s judgment that continued silence could cause harm.
Keep the contrast between remembered injuries and a brother’s comfort in its first-person setting.
shortened: This Wronged One was repeatedly imprisoned, and all have heard of the afflictions that befell Us in the land of Mim.

Beyond all this, consider the oppression and tyranny of My brother and his followers. Wherever We went, before many days had passed, he would come and dwell in perfect comfort and honor with his known women companions - as all have heard and know - protected beneath the pavilions of protection. Yet they call him the wronged one and attribute injustice to God, exalted be His glory!

order.why: Hear the pain attributed to receiving a letter and a request for revelation.
Retain the source’s internal omission in its expression of suffering.
Read the comparison with Joseph and his brothers as a scriptural interpretation of suffering.
Consider the account of movements and disguises after the Bab’s martyrdom.
Read the related account alongside the two years in Sulaymaniyya.
Retain the particular account of concealment and departure for Karbila.
shortened: When Nabil discovered that the flame which had once been kindled and tended there was almost out, that the believers were few, that Yahya had crawled into a secret hole where he lay torpid and inert, and that a wintry cold had taken over--he found himself obliged to leave, bitterly grieving, for Karbila.

order.why: Consider the account of conditions during withdrawal and return.
shortened: From the earliest dawn of the Morn of divine guidance, Adhirbayjan raised aloft the banner of faith and certitude, and the Cause of God thereby spread far and wide. But following the martyrdom of the Exalted One, the journey of the Blessed Beauty from Iraq to Kurdistan, and the seclusion of Yahya in a corner of oblivion, the Cause of God sank deep into apathy everywhere, even in Adhirbayjan. Only a few souls remained steadfast and calm until the Day-Star of the world returned to Iraq and the splendours of His light shone upon all regions in the plenitude of their glory.

order.why: Keep the reported shoe-selling episode in its own narrative voice.
shortened: Mirza Yahya, who claimed to be the Vicegerant of the Bab, always fearing from his own shadow, was concealing himself in a thousand hiding-places. Completely disguised and under the assumed name of Haji Ali, he traveled like a Darveesh between Bagdad and Balsorah. In order to hide his identity from the public he had hung on a piece of string a few red and yellow Arabian slippers, selling them to the people while walking through the streets and Bazaars.

order.why: Read the separate reported account of changing names and occupation.
shortened: In Baghdad, Mirza Yahya was selling Yemeni cloth in the Suq al-Shuyukh, wearing a turban as large as Mount Abu Qubays. Then he changed his name and became known as Haji Ali the cloth merchant. Is that not so, Aqa Husayn? (Bowing) They had asked him, "Why do you change your name every day and wear different clothes each day?" He had replied, "So that people won't recognize me." With such cowardice and foolishness he wanted to oppose the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Retain the reported Najaf episode as a distinct recollection.
Read the contrast between concealment and openly facing enemies.
Consider the contrast between public clamor and absence from gatherings.
shortened: Be not agitated by the clamour of the Yahya'is and others. These affairs are like unto the foam upon the sea: they come and they pass away. As for the Yahya'is, it is in no wise suitable that they should be present in your gatherings, for their sole aim is to cast doubts.

order.why: Keep the reported response to hardships in its historical setting.
Read the reported petition and rupture in Adrianople.
Consider the account of nomination and involvement with the Persian ambassador.
shortened: They found a means and an instrument in the person of Mirza Yahya, the nominee of the Bab. His Excellency the Ambassador used this undiscerning individual as his chief instrument for stirring up mischief. Mirza Yahya had fondly imagined that if the Lamp of the Realm of Glory could be removed from its niche in the West, this new Cause and its flood of abounding grace would be reduced to naught. He therefore joined forces with the Ambassador and began, both overtly and covertly, to stir up a myriad storms of mischief and sedition.

order.why: Keep the account of Siyyid Muhammad’s mission and its consequences attributed.
shortened: This episode is similar in every respect to that of Yahya. He too imagined that his sedition would cause harm and injury to the Blessed Beauty. It was for this reason that he sent Siyyid Muhammad to Constantinople and resorted to innumerable ploys and devices, until at last he exposed Baha'u'llah to great danger. But as soon as the fire of rebellion blazed, it immediately consumed Yahya's own home.

order.why: Retain the concise allegation of a plot in Iraq.
Read the account of the first death threat in its source’s voice.
shortened: When my call was raised, the first servant who sought to shed my blood was my brother, whom I had nurtured over successive years and protected beneath the wing of my favor through the nights and days.

order.why: Consider the allegation of a concealed decree and reversed accusations.
Read the contrast between upbringing and attempted violence.
Keep the viper image as polemical metaphor for betrayal.
Consider protection and elevation followed by alleged conspiracy.
shortened: When he witnessed his own powerlessness, he then slandered this Youth, though thou knowest We had taught him, reared him, and protected him through all months and years. By God! We exalted his mention that he might aid his Lord, yet he chose to veil his face in fear for himself. When the breezes of assurance wafted from Our presence, he then arose to plot in such wise as would astound every person of keen insight. Thus did it befall the Youth from him who was created by His word and was raised up by His command, and God is cognizant of all things.

order.why: Retain the related serpent imagery as the source’s judgment.
Read the seasonal shelter metaphor without adopting it as an editorial label.
shortened: Verily, We sheltered the speckled serpent in winter beneath My tent, yet when the sun of summer shone forth it stirred and bit Me for the first time - to this do honored servants bear witness.
God knoweth that each month he would flee to some quarter in fear for himself, but when the Cause was exalted he emerged and conspired with one of My servants against Me - yet the people know not.

order.why: Consider the image of cutting the Tree after receiving its protection.
Keep the concise reference to whisperings and intrigue within this sequence.
shortened: Through various whisperings and intrigues he prevented people from the Lord of mankind, and through previous delusions led some astray.

order.why: Read the opposition beside the call to stand with wisdom and counsel.
shortened: We stood firm against the enemies in days wherein the feet of every mighty soul did slip, and We disputed with the peoples with wisdom and counsel until We made manifest the Cause through My being alone, and God is witness to what I say. And verily when My brother felt secure in himself he contended against My Self and disputed My verses, until he arose to slay Me.

order.why: Consider the contrast between revelation and the brother’s opposition.
shortened: When my brother witnessed that the sun of certitude had dawned from the horizon of utterance through this Youth, Who stood at the center of all creation with the adornment of the All-Merciful, he emerged from behind the veil of concealment and rose up to war against the Beauty of the All-Glorious, becoming one of the antagonists. He pronounced against me what his self and passion commanded him.

order.why: Read the relation drawn between exalted station and pride.
Examine how names and station are presented as possible sources of delusion.
shortened: He had a brother who protected Him for a number of years and taught Him a letter from the Tablet of the Command. Through this he grew proud before God Who had created him by the word of His command, and became one of the transgressors. The names so deluded him that he sought to slay his Brother without any proof from God or any enlightening Book.

order.why: Consider the account of copying verses followed by pride.
shortened: By God the Truth! He would stand before Us while We recited the verses to him, and he would write them down morning and evening. But when he uttered a word of his own he grew proud against God and desired what he desired with a tyranny that was in the Tablet mighty.

order.why: Read the declaration of independent revelation within the dispute over authority.
Examine the appeal to revealed verses as a proof of Manifestation.
Read creative revelation and sovereignty in the Tablet’s own theological terms.
shortened: Follow ye not in the footsteps of those who, when the verses of God are recited unto them, wax proud against them, notwithstanding that by a single letter thereof have been created the realities of the people of the Divine Realm, then the realities of the people of the Realm of Dominion, then the souls of the people of the Kingdom and the Abha Realm, then whatsoever was and whatsoever shall be, if ye be of those who know. And I am He Who was powerful over whatsoever I willed, and I shall be powerful over whatsoever I desire. Never shall the wiles of the crafty withhold Me from My sovereignty, the All-Powerful, the Almighty, the Omnipotent.

order.why: Consider the argument about the Bayan and vicegerency with its source limits visible.
shortened: By God! Despite his deeds no one opposed him - he rejected himself through turning away from the Truth Who created through His Word.

Never in the Bayan was there mention of successorship or vicegerency. According to you these are the words of the people of the Furqan. What was mentioned in the Bayan was the mention of Letters and Mirrors, and in all instances He declareth that the Mirrors were not and will not be limited.

order.why: Keep the reported explanation of letters addressed from God to God in its own voice.
shortened: These people are following their false imaginings. They say that the letter from the Bab to Yahya begins thus: 'From God, the Mighty, the Beloved, to God, the Mighty, the Beloved.' But this passage is also written at the beginning of the letter to Dayyan and to others.

order.why: Retain the internal omission in the account of a name used as a veil.
Read the criticism of the people of the Bayan as forceful polemic.
Examine the detailed account of the proposed meeting at the Sultan Selim mosque.
Read the related proclamation concerning the public challenge.
Keep the separate statement that no challenger appeared.
shortened: Say: Remember ye the Day of Mubahalih in the Land of Mystery, when the Dawning Place of Inspiration came forth from the precincts of the House, directing His steps toward the House of God, the Lord of all men. We arrived therein while no one else entered it.

order.why: Turn toward the invitation to ponder opponents’ words.
Hear the warning against being content with conjecture.
shortened: Say: O servants! I swear by the Sun of the morn of holy transcendence that what he has mentioned is pure falsehood and he had no purpose except to cast hatred of this servant into hearts.

Although every person of insight perceives that all he has written about this servant has been and will be pure lies and calumny, since not all people possess insight, they must not be content with conjecture.

order.why: Read the problem of followers who relied on accounts of events they had not seen.
shortened: He wrote tablets and sent them in all directions, attributing to this servant that which he himself had done, for he is confident that the ignorant masses of the earth will accept as true and established whatever he says, although they have properly understood this matter, as most have not seen him and whatever they have heard was from this servant.

order.why: Consider the stated limits of the sister’s firsthand knowledge.
Keep affection based on indirect knowledge distinct from witnessed events.
shortened: Tell your sister that if her lack of love stems from love for Yahya, God and all in the heavens and earth bear witness that you had and have no knowledge of his cause, and whatever you have heard was all due to wisdom.

order.why: Read the distinction between reputation and actual connection.
Consider the invitation to travel, see, and hear personally.
Read the parallel invitation to visit Cyprus alongside its polemical claims.
shortened: Although this person is known and visible, let the seekers at least take the trouble to hasten to Cyprus to see with their own eyes his condition and the state of his children, and hear with their own ears his stammering tongue and statements devoid of explanation - no utterance, no exposition, no wisdom, no mysteries, no novel remembrances. If they cannot go there, let them inquire of the people of Cyprus whether that deluded soul, despite his freedom, has in forty years converted or transformed even a single person in that island, or shown any sign of power in any matter.

order.why: Retain the reported invitation to inspect conditions while attributing its judgments about the family.
shortened: Yahya is in Cyprus and his son, Ridvan-'Ali, has joined a [Christian] church. His other son, Ahmad, has become Protestant. His other children are all immersed in troubled-waters of their own and have become a cause of embarrassment. It is good for you to go and witness the misfortune and remorse that is their lot.
Regardless, it is good to go and see for yourself. Cyprus is near, not far. See under what conditions he lives.

order.why: Consider the invitation to examine books held in a London library.
shortened: Observe the copies of books and treatises by Mirza Yahya in the public library in London that exist in his own handwriting and the handwriting of his son, and show them to Taqizadeh so that he may know what an amazingly learned, eloquent and articulate person is promoting nonsense.

order.why: Distinguish the allegations of murder from the proposed documentary and personal sources for investigating them.
Keep the allegations concerning the Bab’s widow and named victims in their source’s voice.
shortened: Despite there being several women in his household, most of whom are known by name and reputation, yet he did not spare the honor of the Primal Point, may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake.

Similarly, for the sake of two days of worldly life, he caused the martyrdom of Dayyan and Khalilu'r-Rahman, sending a woman to the government house for begging. He ordered the execution of the honored Mirza 'Ali-Akbar, who was reportedly one of the relatives of the Exalted One (the Bab), and had him martyred.

order.why: Preserve the omission in the account of reversed blame and named victims.
shortened: O worldly scholar, dust be upon thy head! How strange that contrary matters are witnessed in thee: the oppressor became oppressed, the oppressed became oppressor. Yahya [...] committed treachery against the purity of the Point and martyred His Holiness the Dayyan, and named him and His Holiness Khalil as the "father of evils" and "father of calamities."

order.why: Read the allegations about marriages as the author’s account.
shortened: That is, after the martyrdom of the Bab, he wedded the wife of the Exalted One, the Mother of the Faithful, marriage to whom had, according to His explicit statement, been forbidden to all. And as if that dishonour were not enough, when he found her not to his liking, he presented that honourable lady---the sister of Mulla Rajab-'Ali and the wife of the Bab---to Siyyid Muhammad-i-Isfahani. This was the extent of his exertions, his claim to might, power, and fame: to busy himself, by day and by night, in multiplying the number of his wives.

order.why: Keep the particular family relationship and marriage claim attributed.
shortened: In Adrianople, since the great aunt had connections to Yahya, solely to please him she strove until she gave that poor one to the son of the Prime Minister, Mirza 'Ali Khan.

order.why: Retain the separate list of alleged marriages and its surrounding polemic.
shortened: After the Bab's breast became the target of a thousand bullets, instead of spending his days with weeping eyes and a burning heart and lamentations, he occupied himself with multiplying wives. What is known, evident and confirmed is that he took eleven wives - one named Haji, another the sister of Haji Ruqiyyih, the daughter of Mulla Abdul-Fattah, Ruqiyyih A'raj daughter of Mirza Haydar-Quli, the mother of Ahmad, Badri Jan, Nisa Jan in Tehran, Qanih, an Arab girl, the teacher's wife, and the wife of the Primal Point.

order.why: Keep the related reported marriage account distinct from the written sources.
Attribute the reported allegations concerning sexual conduct and killing.
shortened: Yahya, despite keeping himself constantly hidden and meeting with no one, would become uncontrollable when matters concerning women arose.
Yahya incited others and they strangled Abu'l-Qasim.

order.why: Read the account of disguises, marriages, and letters with attention to its varied claims.
shortened: But how obstinate was Yahya the Envious, who after the martyrdom of the Exalted One (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him), fled out of fear of sacrifice and disguised himself in a dervish cloak, and along the way resorted to begging to protect himself, making like an ant his nest in the hole of obscurity and lethargy.

He wrote seven letters to seven martyrs, requesting from each a virgin, and when his purpose was not achieved, he grew bold and impudent, laying hands on the chaste Mother of the Believers, taking as wife the second consort of the Exalted One despite the explicit prohibition in the Book, and not satisfied with that, after a few days gave her to the rejected Siyyid Muhammad.

order.why: Preserve the source’s omission in the discussion of Cyprus and claimed vicegerency.
Consider the stated claim of evidence for deception.
shortened: These two Iranians who have come to the Hawaiian Islands and America - you should outwardly treat them with kindness. From the evidence, they are Yahyais, meaning followers of the Enemy of God, but they practice deception.

order.why: Read the contrast between confinement and religious influence as an argument about spiritual efficacy.
shortened: One who is so impotent that, despite being in Cyprus with British freedom, could not guide a single soul in forty years - such a one seeks to set up someone against the Blessed Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for the dust of His threshold), Who moved East and West, Whose fame of greatness encompassed all regions, and Whose might became world-conquering; Who, from prison, issued those potent tablets to the kings of the earth, and spread the musk-laden breeze of truth throughout East and West. Yahya, with such impotence and weakness, wishes to resist the Most Glorious Beauty?

order.why: Keep judgments about the children and their conduct attributed to the source.
Retain the harsh polemical address as historical source language.
shortened: Some followers of that unknown one, even though they saw this with their own eyes, still did not awaken, thus proving they are like cattle who follow every caller and incline with every wind. The misguiding guide repeatedly denounced the Exalted One from pulpits in Isfahan. Now he should at least feel shame and no longer mention the name of His Cause. Despite this audacity and wretchedness he considers himself the greater idol after the greatest idol. Therefore take heed, O people of insight.

order.why: Read the language of shunning and punishment within the dispute’s theological framing.
shortened: Be thou steadfast in the love of thy Lord, then detach thyself from the idolaters. And shouldst thou see the Satan from whom thou perceivest the stench of misbelief, shun him and be under mighty protection. He appears in human form and speaks of what was revealed in the Bayan, that he might cause confusion among Our weak servants. Say: Should anyone manifest the essence of piety and worship his Lord with the devotion of both worlds, yet not believe in this Revelation, God will render his deeds void and return him to his abode in hellfire.

order.why: Consider the reported account of an individual leaving the Cause.
shortened: In Baghdad, and due to Yahya's words and deeds, he completely turned away from the Cause of God.

order.why: Read the counsel about dedicating time to teaching with its source boundary visible.
shortened: Likewise, now is the time to turn attention to the Yahya'i group. Dedicate all your time to them, perhaps they will turn to the direction of divine bestowal and abandon following one who says "Those whom you invoke besides God will never create even a fly, though they combine together for the purpose.

order.why: Examine the denial of press reports and the detailed allegations of bribery.
shortened: Furthermore, the followers of Yahya have engaged in slanders that are beyond description. Among other things, they have written numerous reports and detailed letters, both signed and unsigned, to the Chihrihnama newspaper claiming that 'Abdu'l-Baha has sent and continues to send large sums to Tehran to bribe others so that Baha'is might gain membership in parliament and destroy the foundation of Islam and completely eliminate the nation, for they have gained great influence both abroad and within.
Among other things, they have written that I sent ten thousand tumans by telegraph to Tehran for this purpose at the beginning of the elections to Haji Ghulam-Rida, and that I continue to send more.

order.why: Keep the particular encounter involving Sadru’l-Ulama in its historical setting.
shortened: Make people understand that Sadru'l-Ulama is one of his companions and is an Azali, and the son of Sadru'l-Ulama is a pure Azali. This silence of yours has caused their audacity. The Azalis arranged this Najaf issue.

order.why: Attribute the source’s claims about political influence and Iran’s condition.
shortened: This party of Yahya, which among all the dispersed parties set everyone against each other so that perhaps in this struggle they might snatch the ball from the field and establish a government, has ruined Iran. Now they are honored and respected while this oppressed party, from whom nothing has emerged except the good of all, has become captive to the corruption of Iran's ill-wishers.

order.why: Read the distinction between parties and its sweeping national judgment as the source’s argument.
shortened: And finally it became clear and evident that among all parties, the Baha'i party was right and other parties were wrong, especially the shameless party that caused the ruin of Iran.

order.why: Keep the accusation of bribed spies and the reference to Fezzan attributed.
shortened: One moment he would cry out "O what a living!" and the next breath he would cry "O what a reading!" Sometimes he would lavish the worthless treasures of the world upon worldly people so they would become the cause of persecution and cruelty, and sometimes he would present gifts to shameless spies so they would create sedition and corruption and cast 'Abdu'l-Baha into the desert of Fezzan.

order.why: Use the reported distinction between two periods of crisis to separate later disputes.
shortened: At one time, after the Martyrdom of the Bab, the Cause of God suffered a severe blow through the rebellion of Yahya, at another time it sustained intense harm following the ascension of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Read the accusations involving Muhammad Ali and consular authorities as a later episode.
Recounts the activities and alliances of Azal’s sons-in-law.
Keep the comparison with Mirza Yahya from collapsing different historical actors into one.
shortened: In any case, they sent Jamal from here to the Iranian consul in Damascus to create corruption, and from there to Istanbul to the ambassador to cause sedition - exactly like the actions and behavior of Mirza Yahya who sent Siyyid Muhammad to the Iranian ambassador in Istanbul and created those corruptions. Now the Covenant-breakers are also following that same pattern exactly.

order.why: Consider the conditional relationship between Branch status and fidelity to the Covenant.
Retain the reported account of concealed letters in its later setting.
shortened: I asked him, 'Did you really write and dispatch them?' And when he answered that he had, I said, 'I swear by the Righteousness of God! A day will come when Mirza Muhammad-`Ali will wish that his fingers had been cut off so that he could not have taken the pen to proclaim his break with the Covenant. For four years, I have concealed this matter so that the beloved of God may not learn of your unfaithfulness to the Covenant. It is now beyond My power to hide it any longer. You have announced it yourselves to the believers.'"

order.why: Read the reported concern with ambition and material power.
shortened: He said, in substance: Mohammed Ali had a great opportunity given him, but through his ambitions he became false and lost it. Baha'Ollah knew long before the Kitab el Adh was written that Mohammed Ali was intriguing for power and material worldly influence.

order.why: Consider the reported image of returning followers and renewed love.
shortened: Many of those who followed Muhammad- 'Ali are coming back. After the departure of Baha'u'llah all the beautiful blossoms upon the Tree of Life were destroyed by Muhammad- 'Ali and must now be grown again by the Love of 'Abdu'l-Baha.

order.why: Keep the reported confrontation with Aqa Jan distinct from the earlier rupture.
Retain the separate reported account of pride involving Aqa Jan.
shortened: In any case, at the time when Mirza Aqa Jan should have attained the good-pleasure of the Blessed One, at the critical moment, he lost himself because he imagined that this elevated station was of his own doing. In the latter days he had carried his audacity to such a degree that, in the presence of the Blessed Beauty, he had said: "Had His Holiness the Exalted One been in my place, He would not have endured it."

order.why: Read the reported encounter with a woman who distinguished among family members.
Consider the reported understanding of the Covenant as protection against competing claims.
shortened: Similarly, had it not been for the power of the Covenant after the ascension of the Ancient Beauty, it is evident what the people would have done, how they would have spent their time, like Mirza Yahya, taking many wives and satisfying their lusts and desires.

order.why: Read the source’s account of different opponents joining together.
shortened: The enmity of these souls toward the Baha'is has become famous throughout the horizons and its fame has reached the seven layers.
In any case, Jamal al-Din and these persons joined hands.

order.why: Return to the brief statement of protection followed by denial.
Close with the prayer for protection and its scriptural recollections.
shortened: Say: whosoever desires to protect himself, let him read this verse at night and at morn: "O God, my God, I ask Thee by Thy name whereby Thou didst protect Abraham from the fire and Moses from Pharaoh and Baha from Yahya, to guard me from the wicked ones among Thy creatures.

questions: How does the opening refusal of retaliation shape your reading of the accusations that follow?
What different kinds of evidence are offered by first-person writings, reported conversations, documents, and invitations to visit or investigate?
How can readers acknowledge the sources’ anguish while examining their polemical judgments carefully?
What distinguishes claims based on titles or appointment from the forms of spiritual authority argued for in these readings?
How does Qur’an 5:28 illuminate the relationship between religious conviction and refusal of violence?
What practices might help a community remember conflict truthfully while resisting conjecture, inherited hostility, and renewed division?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 5:28 · Refusing to raise a hand
references.note: Read Pickthall’s rendering of the refusal to raise a hand to kill, grounded in fear of the Lord of the Worlds. The compilation itself invokes this verse in the Suriy-i-Sultan. Consider how a scriptural voice becomes part of a response to perceived betrayal, without treating the comparison as independent verification of the historical accusations.

subjects.displayTitle: The station of the Báb: recognition, revelation, and a promised dawn
subjects.introduction: A believer once travelled to meet the Báb and nearly missed Him, because he was looking for a green turban and the Báb had put on a Persian cap.That moment carries a serious question: how does anyone recognize a Manifestation of God when the signs they were taught to expect are absent? The Báb answered with verses that flowed like a river, and His station unfolds from there: the Gate, the promised Qá’im, the Primal Point in whom letters, words and whole books lie folded, the Herald of a Beauty still to come. Bahá’u’lláh calls Him the Morn of Truth, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá holds His lordship and His heralding together. John the Baptist, pointing past himself to one mightier, offers a kindred figure [1], though the Báb’s own claim reaches further. Yet the same light that illumined all things turned, with astonishing humility, toward Him Whom God shall make manifest. To follow that turning is to enter the Bayán, to stand beside the Letters of the Living, and to approach the mystery of twin Manifestations whose dawns were almost one.
subjects.arc: Begin with the puzzle of recognition, move through the Báb’s claims and the imagery of the Primal Point, then explore His announcement of a further revelation and its implications for devotion and conduct.

order.why: Introduce the historical narrative’s own warning about conflicting accounts before its life episodes.
shortened: Touching the individual known as the Bab and the true nature of this sect diverse tales are on the tongues and in the mouths of men, and various accounts are contained in the pages of Persian history and the leaves of European chronicles. But because of the variety of their assertions and the diversity of their narratives not one is as worthy of confidence as it should be. Some have loosed their tongues in extreme censure and condemnation; some foreign chronicles have spoken in a commendatory strain; while a certain section have recorded what they themselves have heard without addressing themselves either to censure or approbation.
The Bab was a young merchant of the Pure Lineage.
On account of what was observed in Him He was noted for godliness, devoutness, virtue, and piety, and was regarded in the sight of men as so characterized.

order.why: Open with the reported encounter in which expectation of a green turban complicates recognition.
Hear the warning against allowing others’ deeds to obscure recognition.
Read the account of a believer bringing doubts for an answer.
Hear the reported declaration of the Promised One at the examination in Tabriz.
shortened: I am, I am, I am, the promised One! I am the One whose name you have for a thousand years invoked, at whose mention you have risen, whose advent you have longed to witness, and the hour of whose Revelation you have prayed God to hasten.

order.why: Examine the account of successive declarations of station.
Distinguish the promised Qa’im within the Qur’anic dispensation from the Primal Point and Herald in the new dispensation.
Read morning light and heralding together.
shortened: The Bab, the Exalted One, is the Morn of Truth, the splendour of Whose light shineth through all regions. He is also the Harbinger of the Most Great Light, the Abha Luminary.

order.why: Consider the explicit conjunction of lordship and heralding.
Read the distinction between the two Manifestations and Abdu’l-Baha’s servitude.
shortened: For the sincere belief of 'Abdu'l-Baha is this: that the Primal Point, His Holiness the Exalted One - may my spirit be sacrificed for Him - is the Manifestation of Supreme Lordship and the Herald of the Beauty of Abha and the Sun of Truth and the Essence of Singleness and the Revelation of Divinity, the Most Great Luminary of the higher world, the Beauty of Abha, and 'Abdu'l-Baha is the weak, mortal servant of those two peerless Stars.

order.why: Keep the correction of a description that did not accord with Abdu’l-Baha’s stated belief.
Explore the Persian Bayan’s account of the Primal Will and revealed verses.
shortened: Whoso knoweth of a certainty that He is the Point of the Qur'an manifested in His Resurrection, and the Point of the Bayan in His first Revelation, and that He is the Primal Will Who existeth by Himself, the Self-Subsistent, while all things are created by His bidding, and exist by Him, he is numbered among those whose inmost realities have testified unto the unity of his Lord.

Were all the people that dwell on earth to assemble together, they would be unable to produce a single verse like unto the ones which God hath caused to stream forth from the tongue of the Point of the Bayan. Indeed, if any living creature were to pause to meditate he would undoubtedly realize that these verses are not the work of man, but are solely to be ascribed unto God, the One, the Peerless, Who causeth them to flow forth from the tongue of whomsoever He willeth, and hath not revealed nor will He reveal them save through the Focal Point of God's Primal Will. He it is, through Whose dispensations divine Messengers are raised up and heavenly Books are sent down.

order.why: Read the Epistle’s declaration of the Primal Point with its source omissions visible.
shortened: The essence of all remembrance is that

I am the Primal Point from which have been generated all created things. I am the Countenance of God Whose splendor can never be obscured, the Light of God Whose radiance can never fade. Whoso recognizeth Me, assurance and all good are in store for him, and whoso faileth to recognize Me, infernal fire and all evil await him.…

order.why: Consider the argument from the circumstances and rapidity of revelation.
Read the comparison of periods of revelation as the source’s theological argument.
shortened: When the Cause hath reached unto God, look not upon your proofs, for all this hath been revealed by God. Were ye to reflect upon what hath been revealed, that which God revealed in twenty-three years is now revealed in four days.

order.why: Follow the appeal to verses and the Seven Proofs.
Keep the related account of demands for supernatural signs in its separate wording.
Explore Joseph, the Word of Unity, and the bearing of divine authority.
shortened: God hath indeed exalted Joseph through Our name, and God hath made him in the Book a guardian, stationed around the Fire.

God hath made Joseph and his brethren the Word of Unity, and the All-Merciful hath ordained them as twelve letters, and this Word hath been inscribed in the Mother Book with thy Lord, written in the Line around the Line.
God offered Our authority to the heavens, earth and mountains; they refused to bear it and were afraid of it. But man -- God's Great Remembrance, this Ali -- undertook it.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s language of creation through the speaker.
Read recognition and veiling in the visitation Tablet’s voice.
Consider the manifestation of the Gate and its language of judgment.
shortened: I have manifested the Gate through the revelation of My Self on the Day of Resurrection, that We might recompense those who believed in the Qur'an and cast into the fire those who believed not therein.

order.why: Place servanthood beside divine splendor.
shortened: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, the Mighty, the Beauteous, and that the Point of the Bayan is His servant and His splendor unto all who are in the heavens and on earth.

order.why: Read the parallel testimony to servant and Glory.
Consider names, attributes, and decree in relation to recognition.
shortened: O Rida, bear thou witness in thy soul and being, with the tongue which God hath placed within thee, that there is none other God but Him, and that He Who was sent with the name of 'Ali is verily the Truth from His presence, though most of the people perceive it not.
Through Him appeared the Kingdom of Names and Attributes, and by Him was distinguished every irrevocable decree from God, the Mighty, the Self-Subsisting.

order.why: Keep the declaration of a distinctive station explicit.
Read the Tree of the Bayan and the divine voice as theological imagery.
Consider the reported divine declaration in every state.
shortened: O Hasan! Say: O deniers! The Herald, that is, the Primal Point, hath declared: "Verily, in every state He speaketh: 'I, verily, am God. There is none other God but Me, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.'"

order.why: Explore how the point becomes letters, words, and a book, then returns to its center.
shortened: Praise be to God Who created and brought forth a comprehensive, perfect, all-encompassing Point, possessing and containing all universal meanings in the world of existence, wherein all realities, effects and ordinances are integrated and included through simplicity and unity, calling to oneness in all affairs in the realm of being.

Then it became detailed, multiplied, branched out and was explained, and revolved in the circle of letters, appearing in the most wonderful forms, becoming a magnet for its spirits, and manifesting with the most beautiful beauty in all ranks and stations.

Then it returned and came back to its center in the praiseworthy station. Through its rotation, movement, inclination, beginning and return, the perfect words and exalted letters were realized, and the clear verses were arranged. Thus appeared the Preserved Tablet, the Inscribed Book, and the Outstretched Parchment.

order.why: Read the expansion from point to innumerable books.
shortened: We have made manifest the Point and have expounded it until there appeared books which none can reckon save the All-Knowing.

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of the point, letters, and nineteen in its source’s voice.
shortened: In the dogmatic teachings about the Qur'an, called Hadith, it says: "Everything that is in the Qur'an lies in the first Surih, the Fatihah, and everything that is in the Fatihah is to be found in the first sentence: Bismi'llahi'r-Rahmani'r-Rahim = in the Name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, and everything in this first sentence is contained in the "bi" (its initial letter), and everything contained in the "bi" is to be found in the point under the "bi" (its smallest part), and I (the Prophet, here 'Ali) (successor and interpreter of Muhammad and the Qur'an) am the Point (Nuqtih) under the "bi"." - His Holiness the Bab has found from counting the letters of the phrase: Bismi'llahi'r-Rahmani'r-Rahim that the number 19 represents the mystic basic number of the cosmos (universe). This mystic basic number 19 at the same time represents the Logos, the Manifestation, the Emanation of God, which can at the same time be designated by the "bi" or the point (nuqtih) under the "bi".

order.why: Consider the unexpected movement from letters and point to darkness and a fisher.
shortened: How exalted and powerful, that He referred all letters to the Word, and the Word to the Point, and the Point to a speck of darkness, and made that darkness a Fisher, giving it dwelling on the shore of the sea of eternity!

order.why: Hear the blessing of the Point around whom creation revolves.
shortened: Do Thou bless, O Lord my God, the Primal Point, through Whom the point of creation hath been made to revolve in both the visible and invisible worlds, Whom Thou hast designated as the One whereunto should return whatsoever must return unto Thee, and as the Revealer of whatsoever may be manifested by Thee.

order.why: Read the extended prayer’s names for the Primal Point and His announcing role.
Consider the prayer’s distinction between the Primal Point and the first believer.
Read the visitation prayer’s invocation of the Point and the signs of divine names.
Keep the praise of the first believer distinct from the station of the Manifestation.
Hear the imagery of guidance, flame, and illumination.
Read the point of heaven and attraction toward the Root.
Consider the image of a balance giving things their measure.
Keep the metaphorical account of motion and winds within its spiritual context.
Read the summons to perceive the light of the divine countenance.
Hear the concise image of drawing aside a veil.
Read the Primal Point’s appearance in the final revolution.
Consider continuity of voice in the latter Manifestation, preserving the source’s boundary.
shortened: Say: Verily the Primal Point, in His latter Manifestation, speaketh with the Most Glorious tongue, saying: "O people! Did We not give you glad tidings of My appearance after Me?

order.why: Retain the question addressed to those who deny the appearance.
shortened: Say: He hath appeared as 'Ali appeared aforetime. Open your eyes that ye may behold Him now upon this most luminous horizon, speaking forth the truth with a sorrowful voice saying: "Do ye deny, O people, Him Who created you from dust, then from a drop of fluid, and made you complete beings?

order.why: Examine humility and exalted claims together in the argument of the Kitab-i-Badi.
shortened: And furthermore He says: "Glory be unto Thee, O my God! How insignificant is my mention and whatever is attributed to me when I wish to ascribe it unto Thee. Accept me and whatever is attributed to me through Thy grace, for Thou art the best of those who show grace."
O heedless ones among the people of the Bayan! Despite such humility from the Primal Point regarding His subsequent manifestation, you remain unaware and occupy yourselves with such utterances.

As He states in one place - exalted be His mention: "Say: I have descended to where I said I am an atom and less than an atom, just as I have said I am the Lord and Creator of every possessor of lordship..."

order.why: Read the Point’s dependence upon Him Whom God shall make manifest.
shortened: Indeed ye have been called into being through the power of the Point of the Bayan while the Point Himself is resigned to the Will of Him Whom God shall make manifest, is exalted through His transcendent sublimity, is sustained by the evidences of His might, is glorified by the majesty of His oneness, is adorned by the beauty of His singleness, is empowered by His eternal dominion and is invested with authority through His everlasting sovereignty.

order.why: Consider the hope of being mentioned by the promised Manifestation.
Read the related statement about being mentioned once in the holy court.
Hear the warning that the promised One cannot be encompassed by earlier allusions.
Keep the parallel statement in its separate source wording.
shortened: The Primal Point - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - states: "I have written an essence regarding His mention, which is that He cannot be known through My allusion nor through what was revealed in the Bayan."

order.why: Retain the source’s omission while reading its claim of sanctification from earlier formulations.
shortened: He made mention of Me after He had established through clear proof the sanctification of My Being from whatsoever was revealed in the Bayan, saying: "I have written a gem concerning His remembrance: He shall not be referred to by My reference nor by what hath been revealed in the Bayan." Thus did speak He Who sacrificed His spirit in My straight and manifest path...

order.why: Consider the assertion that the entire Bayan cannot resist a word of the promised revelation.
shortened: But the Bab - may my spirit be a sacrifice unto Him - left no veil for the people of the Bayan. He declared that whatever the Desired Beauty would reveal would be the truth, and that all of the Bayan and its contents could not resist even one of His words.

order.why: Read the injunction not to pause at the time of manifestation.
shortened: He counseled you throughout the Bayan not to pause at the time of His manifestation for anything created between the heavens and earth.

order.why: Distinguishes the Bab’s independent station from that of His followers.
Explore the extended exhortation to recognize the promised One beyond inherited expectations.
shortened: Then We raised up the Sovereign of the Messengers, who was named Ali in all the tablets, and through him We opened the gates of grace unto the faces of all created things. We made him the herald of this Manifestation. He said: "O people! When the Beloved of the worlds cometh unto you, beware lest ye hesitate in His Manifestation and cling to what ye possess from the tidings of the ancients. Verily, I have revealed the Bayan for His sake and made it as a leaf among the leaves of Paradise for Him. Beware lest ye differ concerning His wondrous Cause. Follow not your leaders at the time of His appearance, for on that Day the affairs of the worlds shall be changed, and the followers of the Mount shall perish at the dawning of a drop from that crimson Light rising from the Most Glorious Horizon. Fear God and be not of them that are veiled.

order.why: Read the Bayan as a means of preventing deprivation of recognition.
shortened: In any case, the Primal Point - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - in view of the existence of this Manifestation and its dawning in those days, completed all the Bayan with this Most Great Remembrance, lest the people of the Bayan be debarred from the All-Merciful.

order.why: Consider the fragrance of the promised revelation in every word of the Bayan.
Read the stated purpose of revealing the Bayan.
shortened: We have counseled the servants through the tongue of the Manifestation of My Self, Whom We made the Herald of this mighty and impregnable Cause. He revealed the Bayan solely for My wondrous remembrance.

order.why: Hear the direct invitation to read the Bayan.
Connect glad tidings, covenant, and sacrifice.
Read beginning and ending the Book with the promised Name.
Keep the declaration of first worship beside its polemical setting.
Consider the distinction between the Manifestation and those who guide others toward Him.
Read the identification of the Youth heralded by earlier Messengers.
shortened: I am indeed the Youth heralded by the Primal Point and, before Him, by the Prophets and Messengers.

order.why: Consider the adornment of the Bayan through the promised One’s name.
Keep the personal address concerning the year Nine and attainment in its own setting.
shortened: O Kamal, thou hast been blessed with two great bounties: First, that in the year Nine thou wast vouchsafed the presence of God, concerning which the Primal Point gave all this glad-tiding in His words: "And in the year Nine ye shall be blessed with attaining the presence of God."

order.why: Hear the dove and pearl imagery of praise and announcement.
Read the particular statement joining Manifestation and Herald.
Consider the announcement of a Manifestation promised in earlier books.
Read the comparison between one word of the promised One and the whole Bayan.
shortened: Say: O people! The Revealer of the Bayan declared: O concourse of creation! Ye were created for His days. Fear God and be not of those who are veiled. Whoso hath attained unto but one word from Him - this is better for him than all that was revealed in the Bayan.

order.why: Hear the stated relationship between the Cause, the Point, and the Bayan.
shortened: Were it not for My Cause, the Point would not have appeared and the Bayan would not have been revealed - to this testifieth he who is powerful in the Cause.

order.why: Read the proclamation of the promised and hidden Treasure.
shortened: And the Author of the Bayan proclaimeth amidst all possibilities, declaring: 'The All-Merciful hath come! He, verily, is the Promised One, the Remembered One, the One inscribed, the Hidden Treasure!'

order.why: Consider the intention attributed to the Point and the Primal Beauty.
Keep the reported morning-star announcement in its own wording.
shortened: Through all the cities that you shall pass, convey to all the friends my wonderful Abha greeting and announce to them:-

Firstly: His Holiness the Supreme (Bab) was the morning star heralding the daybreak; he was the herald proclaiming the approaching arrival of the King of Kings, the messenger bringing the Glad news of the appearance of the Kingdom.

order.why: Read the reported sun-and-moon comparison as spiritual interpretation.
Retain the reported statement about continuous resurrection.
shortened: This is why the Primal Point - may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him - states: "By God! The Hour has come and the moon has been cleft asunder, and all are in continuous resurrection."

order.why: Attribute the reported interpretation of names without treating it as independently established linguistics.
shortened: This was when the Bab came who was Ali Mohamed, and according to the Hebrew language, if we take those two words, Elijah and the prophet, it will mean Ali and Mohammed or Ali Mohammed who is the First Point.

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of the sacrificial address distinct from historical verification.
shortened: Verily, everything in me I sacrifice to Thee and I desire only to be killed in Thy path.' To whom do these addresses in the Ahsan-el-Kessas refer? Undoubtedly to the One-Whom-God-Shall-Manifest, that is His Holiness Baha'u'llah, and not to Mirza Yahya (Ezel).

order.why: Read the appeal to the Bayan in relation to sacrifice.
Consider how remembering sacrifice becomes a warning against repeating earlier rejection.
shortened: Say: "Verily, He Who came unto you by the name of 'Ali was the Herald of this Most Great, Most Glorious Manifestation, and His Most Exalted Pen moved only in My remembrance and praise, and there flowed from His ink naught but this wise Remembrance, until He sacrificed His soul in My love that ye might not commit in the time of the Manifestation what the people of the Furqan, and before them the people of the Torah and the Gospel, committed."

order.why: Read the appeal to the Bab’s suffering beside its criticism of inherited fancies.
shortened: O people! Fear ye God, then be ashamed before Him Who was suspended in the air and sacrificed Himself in the path of God, the Just King, the All-Informed. By God! He sacrificed Himself for naught else but to manifest that which hath been manifested in these days. Yet ye, O people of the Bayan, have remained heedless of that which was intended and have clung to your own idle fancies, without any clear authority or enlightening Book.

order.why: Hear the identification of the Primal Point amid the account of martyrdom.
Read the devotional response to sacrifice in its source’s own intensity.
shortened: Consider how His Holiness the Exalted One - may my spirit and my very being be sacrificed for Him - laid down His life for that All-Effulgent Lamp and guided His lovers to self-sacrifice and martyrdom.
May my spirit, my inner being, my reality, my truth, my identity, my hidden and manifest self be offered up for a single drop of His pure blood.

order.why: Retain the reported supplication about calamities in the path of love.
Turn from remembering sacrifice toward an invitation to follow a heavenly example.
shortened: Consider how the Bab endured difficulties and tribulations; how He gave His life in the Cause of God; how He was attracted to the love of the Blessed Beauty, Baha'u'llah; and how He announced the glad tidings of His manifestation. We must follow His heavenly example; we must be self-sacrificing and aglow with the fire of the love of God.

order.why: Keep the reported choice of Quddus as a pilgrimage companion.
shortened: In this pilgrimage upon which We are soon to embark, We have chosen Quddus as Our companion.

order.why: Read the reported wish to assist Quddus despite imprisonment.
shortened: But for My incarceration in the Jabal-i-Shadid, the fortress of Chihriq, it would have been incumbent upon Me to lend My personal assistance to My beloved Quddus.

order.why: Attribute the account of attaining the Presence and preserve its cross-reference.
shortened: The Herald, that is, the Primal Point - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake - in the days of His journey to Maku, while outwardly veiled from all, attained the honor of His presence, [cf. AB11477] and His Holiness Quddus - upon him be the Most Glorious of all Glory - attained it repeatedly. During the journey to the Land of Kha He specifically summoned him, and for several months he was blessed with attaining His presence.

order.why: Consider the reported distinction between kinship and spiritual relationship.
shortened: Spiritual Relationship is the true Family-hood of God's children. The Bab had many relatives. He particularly wished that His mother should believe in thisRevelation and attain.

order.why: Retain the small detail of frankincense and rock candy as part of the preserved portrait.
Keep the practical description of three framed likenesses in its own setting.
shortened: There are three frames present - two with the blessed likenesses of the Ancient Beauty and one with the blessed likeness of His Holiness the Exalted One, may my spirit be a sacrifice for Their loved ones.

order.why: Read the acknowledgment of an elegy as an act of remembrance.
shortened: O thou who art firm in the Covenant! The elegy that you composed in commemoration of that Pure Light, that Embodied Spirit, that Brilliant Star of the Supreme Concourse, that Sun of the Higher World, the Primal Point - may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him - was reviewed.

order.why: Connect the station with Shiraz as the dawning-place of a new revelation.
Read the exhortation to the homeland through its abundant imagery of knowledge and love.
Close the linked readings with a prayer joining oneness and the promise of a greater Manifestation.
shortened: O my God, my God! These are servants who have turned toward the Kingdom of Thy mercy, have clung to the hem of the robe of Thy oneness, have sincerely turned their faces to Thy beauty, and have believed in Thy unity and in Thy divine Word - the Primal Point and the Most Exalted One - Who gave glad tidings to all on earth and in heaven of Thy Most Great Manifestation, the luminous Sun of Thy Reality.

order.why: End with the supplied account of Siyyid Yahya’s questions and response to a revealed commentary.

questions: What does the green-turban encounter suggest about the difference between recognizing a person and recognizing a spiritual claim?
How do the titles Primal Point, Manifestation, and Herald illuminate different aspects of the Báb’s station in these readings?
What possibilities of meaning open when a point is imagined as containing letters, words, and a book?
How does John’s announcement in Luke 3:15–17 help explore heralding, and where does the compilation invite a different understanding of the Báb’s own authority?
Why might earlier religious knowledge both prepare a person for recognition and become an obstacle to it?
How do the prayers, accounts of companionship, and invitations to follow an example connect theological claims with a reader’s conduct?

references.label: 1 · Luke 3:15–17 · Expectation and the one to come
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of people wondering whether John is the Christ, and John’s announcement of one mightier who will baptize with the Holy Ghost and fire. Compare the act of directing expectation toward another with the Báb’s heralding role. Keep in view the compilation’s additional claim that the Báb is Himself a Manifestation of God; the comparison does not establish identical stations.
